messages:
elaine: noticing a regression on streaming perceived latency after the flush-interval tweak. p95 for short prompts jumped from ~120ms to ~260ms even though aggregate throughput is better. rolling this to canary now, but want eyes on kernel selection + batching interaction.
mike: saw this too on canary-3. kv hit rate dropped from 0.94 to 0.78 for the same workloads. looks like larger microbatches are evicting useful KV prefixes earlier.
jess: interesting — is the regression mostly for first-token or steady-state?
elaine: first-token experience is worse — users report slower initial token drip. steady-state tokens/sec improved ~1.5x. p99 tail however got wider -> 900ms.
infra-bot: deploy canary-3 started by @elaine at 2026-02-13T09:12:25Z :rocket:
natalie: quick profiling: when flush interval = 50ms we batch up to 16 requests -> kernel scheduler picks `matmul-heavy` path. at 20ms we go to 6-8 requests -> `fused-attn` chosen more often. per-kernel latencies: `fused-attn` single-token emit ~18ms, `matmul-heavy` amortized ~12ms per token but has a larger scheduling delay (queueing).
ryan: so higher throughput kernel is lower per-token but increases wait due to batch formation. perceived latency suffers because users wait for the first small chunk.
mike: measurement snippet i ran: ```python
# simulate streaming flush
for flush_ms in [10,20,50]:
  run(flush_ms)
  print(flush_ms, p95_first_token, p95_steady)
```
results: 10ms -> p95_first 90ms, steady 70ms; 20ms -> 120ms/60ms; 50ms -> 260ms/40ms.
jess: KV cache hit drop is the signal — larger batching increases prefix evictions. can we pin KV shards or bump cache size for canary to verify?
elaine: pinned cache + canary repro yields hit 0.92 and p95_first drops to 140ms (still worse than 20ms flush). suggests both KV + kernel scheduling matter.
natalie: proposal: hybrid flush policy: emit a small initial chunk at t=10ms (or after 1 token), then use microflush backoff to 50ms for subsequent tokens. that preserves first-token latency while keeping throughput gains.
ryan: another angle: dynamic microbatch sizing by route SLO. for low-latency routes (chat), cap microbatch to 8; for bulk generation allow bigger batches and choose matmul path. would need routing policy + kernel hints.
mike: we should also add a quick heuristic in scheduler: if estimated time-to-first-token (ETFT) > SLO threshold, prefer `fused-attn` even if throughput delta higher for `matmul`.
jess: agree. also add telemetry tag for chunk-size and flush-interval per request so we can correlate user-perceived latency with server decisions.
elaine: action items: 1) implement hybrid initial-chunk emit (natalie) 2) add KV pin experiment on canary (mike) 3) scheduler heuristic prototype to prefer low-latency kernel when ETFT close to SLO (ryan) 4) add telemetry tags (jess). I'll follow up with a short experiment plan.
mike: noted. I'll spin canary with pinned KV and report numbers in ~2h.
jess: i'll add telemetry fields and a Grafana panel for chunk-size vs p95_first.
natalie: i'll start prototype for hybrid flush; simple: emit 1 token at 10ms then resume normal flush. gives immediate UX improvement without large scheduler changes.
elaine: thanks team :thumbsup: let's sync in #eng-runtime in ~2.5h with results. if anyone has quick wins (config flags) drop them here.
